All five books are confirmed on Project Gutenberg with free full-text online reading. Here's your ranked starter list, drawn from Project Gutenberg's **Classics of Literature** collection (Bookshelf #649).

---

## 🥇 1. The Strange Case of Dr. Jekyll and Mr. Hyde — *Best Starting Point*
- **Author:** Robert Louis Stevenson · **Published:** 1886 · **Genre:** Gothic horror novella
- **PG eBook #43** — [Read online now ✓](https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/43)
- **About:** London lawyer Gabriel Utterson investigates the strange link between his respectable friend Dr. Henry Jekyll and the brutal Edward Hyde, uncovering a disturbing mystery about the duality of human nature.
- **Why #1:** At roughly 60–70 pages it's a single-sitting read, structured as a mystery with a strong forward pull. The prose is clear Victorian English without dense digressions, and the plot arrives at a genuine payoff quickly — so you get the full "I finished a classic" satisfaction with minimal commitment.

## 🥈 2. Alice's Adventures in Wonderland
- **Author:** Lewis Carroll · **Published:** 1865 · **Genre:** Children's fantasy / literary nonsense
- **PG eBook #11** — [Read online now ✓](https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/11) (verified full text, with Tenniel illustrations)
- **About:** A curious girl follows a waistcoated White Rabbit down a rabbit hole into a fantasy world of peculiar talking creatures, playing with logic and language along the way.
- **Why #2:** Short, episodic chapters mean you can stop and start freely, and the vocabulary is genuinely simple. It ranks just below Jekyll only because its nonsense logic has no conventional plot to follow — some new readers find the absence of narrative momentum disorienting rather than delightful.

## 🥉 3. The Hound of the Baskervilles
- **Author:** Arthur Conan Doyle · **Published:** serialized 1901–1902 · **Genre:** Detective / crime novel
- **PG eBook #2852** — [Read online now ✓](https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/2852)
- **About:** Holmes and Watson investigate a centuries-old legend of a demonic hound stalking the Baskerville family on the desolate moors of Dartmoor after Sir Charles dies mysteriously.
- **Why #3:** Doyle writes in brisk, modern-feeling prose built around cliffhangers — it reads like contemporary genre fiction. It's a full-length novel rather than a novella, and Watson's mid-book letters and reports slow the pace, which is why it sits behind the two shorter works.

## 4. Pride and Prejudice
- **Author:** Jane Austen · **Published:** 1813 · **Genre:** Romance / social satire
- **PG eBook #1342** — [Read online now ✓](https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/1342)
- **About:** Elizabeth Bennet must learn to see past first impressions and hasty judgments. With five daughters and an estate that can only pass to male heirs, the Bennets face pressure to marry well — then wealthy Mr. Darcy arrives.
- **Why #4:** The emotional dynamics are timeless and the dialogue is sharp and funny. But it demands more of a beginner: a large cast, long formal sentences, and heavy reliance on early-1800s social rules (entailment, "coming out," calling cards) that need context to land.

## 5. Frankenstein; or, The Modern Prometheus
- **Author:** Mary Wollstonecraft Shelley · **Published:** 1818 · **Genre:** Gothic / early science fiction
- **PG eBook #84** — [Read online now ✓](https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/84)
- **About:** Victor Frankenstein creates a living being from assembled body parts, then flees in horror. The conscious creature must navigate a world that fears him, seeking connection and meeting only rejection — until bitterness turns to revenge.
- **Why #5:** A superb book, but the least beginner-friendly here. It uses a nested "frame narrative" (letters containing Victor's story, which contains the creature's story), lengthy Romantic-era landscape passages, and elevated, philosophical prose that slows the plot considerably.

---

**A note on the ranking:** I deliberately did **not** rank by popularity. By raw download counts on Project Gutenberg, *Pride and Prejudice* (~190k) and *Frankenstein* (~92k) outrank *Alice* and *Jekyll & Hyde* — yet both place lower here because length, sentence complexity, narrative structure, and required historical context matter far more for a first-time reader than fame does.

**Start with *Dr. Jekyll and Mr. Hyde*.** If you enjoy it, *The Hound of the Baskervilles* is the natural next step into full-length Victorian novels.

Nothing was purchased or downloaded — all five are read-in-browser links, and Project Gutenberg titles are public domain and free by design.
